atomic://architecture/layers.description: Every module by height, with the rule that decides which may include which. ReadResourceFile this before adding an include across modules.
atomic://architecture/layers.name: The layer stack

atomic://architecture/modules.description: Every module and program as JSON: tier, layer, what it links, what links it, and the sideways edges each is allowed. The same data the architecture check enforces.
atomic://architecture/modules.name: The module graph

atomic://bindings/luau.description: The type declarations every Luau script in this engine is checked against, and the file script_check uses.
atomic://bindings/luau.name: The Luau declarations

atomic://bindings/manifest.description: Every class, property, enum and datatype a script may name, generated from the class table by `just bindings`. Large - a couple of hundred kilobytes.
atomic://bindings/manifest.name: The scripting manifest

atomic://components.description: Every component type this engine registers, with its size, whether it is a tag, whether a save file can carry it and how many bytes a replication delta needs.
atomic://components.name: The component catalogue

atomic://metadata/audio_observation/v1.description: Metadata for the copied sample-aligned audio record. Waveform bytes stay in digest-addressed chunks fetched through get_audio_waveform_chunk.
atomic://metadata/audio_observation/v1.name: audio_observation/v1 metadata

begin_raw_scene_extract.description: Captures one fenced scene as portable raw mesh and texture sections with an inline manifest.
begin_raw_scene_extract.name: begin_raw_scene_extract

capture.description: Queues one calibrated render capture from a paused world's exact completed snapshot.
capture.name: capture

capture_bundle.description: Queues one data-scene-options/v1 bundle from a paused world's exact completed snapshot.
capture_bundle.name: capture_bundle

capture_multi_camera.description: Queues 2 to 6 named camera captures in one renderer frame from one exact paused world snapshot. The shared renderer frame does not make simulation stepping atomic.
capture_multi_camera.name: capture_multi_camera

checkpoint.description: Retains a restorable checkpoint when the host provides rehydration.
checkpoint.name: checkpoint

class_get.description: One class: what it derives from, and every property it exposes with the type it carries, whether it can be written and whether a script can see it at all. This is the live class table rather than the checked-in manifest, so it describes what this process registered. Use instance_get to read the values off a particular instance.
class_get.name: class_get

class_list.description: Every class this process registers, with what it derives from. A class is what Instance.new names and what a save file carries; its properties are what a script may read and write. Inheritance is set inclusion here, so a query for a base class matches every derived instance. Call class_get for one class's properties.

derivedFrom.description: Only classes that are a kind of this one.

class_list.name: class_list

component_get.description: The values one entity holds for one component, field by field. Null when the entity does not carry it - which is a different answer from carrying it with every field at zero.
component_get.name: component_get

component_list.description: Every component a game declared for itself, with its fields and how many entities in a scene carry it. A component is the storage under the class tree: an instance is an entity and a class is a set of these. Components the engine declares are not listed here - those are reached as properties, through instance_get.
component_list.name: component_list

component_set.description: Writes fields of one component on one entity, adding it when the entity does not carry it yet. Fields left out keep what they had; a fresh component starts at zero. Vector3 and Color3 take an object of named components, as instance_set does.
component_set.name: component_set

data_factory_operation_audit.description: Reads the bounded, redacted replay ledger shared by lifecycle and capture mutation tools. Rows are newest first and contain no raw scene arguments.
data_factory_operation_audit.name: data_factory_operation_audit

engine_components.description: Every component type this engine registers, with its size, whether it is a tag, whether a save file can carry it and whether replication has a compact form for it. A component is the storage under the class tree: an instance is an entity and a class is a set of these. Use component_list instead for the components a game declared for itself, and instance_get to read one off a particular instance.
engine_components.name: engine_components

engine_info.description: This program's own state: how many scenes it holds and what they are called. Call it first.
engine_info.name: engine_info

entity_query.description: Every entity in a scene carrying all of the named components. This is the query a system runs, asked from outside: name the components and get the ids back, then read one with component_get or instance_get.

components.description: Every one an entity must carry. Call component_list first.

entity_query.name: entity_query

export_gltf_scene.description: Exports one fenced scene as a bounded glTF 2.0 GLB. Results above 40 KiB use a retained resource with ranged reads and explicit release. The v1 subset contains built-in, EditableMesh and bounded resident mesh geometry, source image maps, material runs and perspective cameras. Unavailable source facts are listed explicitly.
export_gltf_scene.name: export_gltf_scene

fork_world.description: Forks one retained checkpoint into an isolated, non-presented branch runtime. The parent lifecycle revision and checkpoint identity fence the operation.
fork_world.name: fork_world

get_audio_observation.description: Returns one bounded audio_observation/v1 record. Waveform bytes remain external digest-addressed chunks.
get_audio_observation.name: get_audio_observation

get_audio_waveform_chunk.description: Copies a bounded byte range from one digest-addressed waveform chunk returned by get_audio_observation.
get_audio_waveform_chunk.name: get_audio_waveform_chunk

get_authored_affordances.description: Return bounded explicit authored affordances in stable identity order. Geometry and colliders do not infer semantics.
get_authored_affordances.name: get_authored_affordances

get_authored_navmesh_path.description: Finds a bounded authored-walkable surface route in one retained paused snapshot. A route is returned only for supported authored geometry and a clear zero-radius corridor; every other case is explicitly unknown.
get_authored_navmesh_path.name: get_authored_navmesh_path

get_camera_rendering_data.description: Camera calibration for a stable authored camera id, or the scene's active camera.
get_camera_rendering_data.name: get_camera_rendering_data

get_capture_channels.description: Capture channel capability metadata for one scene.
get_capture_channels.name: get_capture_channels

get_collider_bev.description: Returns a snapshot-bound bird's-eye collider-contact grid. Rows are z-major from minimum Z to maximum Z; columns then run from minimum X to maximum X. Each cell is occupied, empty, or explicitly unknown when physics cannot prove a negative answer.
get_collider_bev.name: get_collider_bev

get_collider_occupancy.description: Tests up to 32 named finite world-space AABBs against the exact completed, retained all-systems-paused snapshot. Boundary contact counts as collider contact. This is not a filled-volume test: unavailable physics, broad-phase overflow, and mesh or hull candidates remain explicitly incomplete.
get_collider_occupancy.name: get_collider_occupancy

get_event_narratives.description: Script-declared, bounded event narratives for one scene.
get_event_narratives.name: get_event_narratives

get_filled_occupancy.description: Returns a bounded snapshot-bound voxel grid. A filled cell is proven only when one analytic collider contains its whole AABB. Collider unions, baked hulls and meshes remain explicitly unknown rather than being inferred.
get_filled_occupancy.name: get_filled_occupancy

get_gltf_scene_chunk.description: Returns up to one MiB from a retained glTF export at its original world revision.
get_gltf_scene_chunk.name: get_gltf_scene_chunk

get_raw_scene_chunk.description: Returns up to one MiB from a retained raw scene extract at its original world revision.
get_raw_scene_chunk.name: get_raw_scene_chunk

get_render_graph.description: Read the installed render graph, compiled schedule, and bounded memory profile.
get_render_graph.name: get_render_graph

get_resource.description: Returns up to one MiB of one retained capture resource as base64.
get_resource.name: get_resource

get_resources.description: Durable resource metadata for one scene.
get_resources.name: get_resources

get_rig_export.description: A bounded data-rig/v1 export of identified skeletons. Missing engine source data is declared rather than inferred.
get_rig_export.name: get_rig_export

get_scene_snapshot.description: A read-only snapshot of one scene using stable authored ids. Large results return an immutable resource for get_scene_snapshot_chunk and release_scene_snapshot.
get_scene_snapshot.name: get_scene_snapshot

get_scene_snapshot_chunk.description: Returns at most 32768 bytes of the retained exact snapshot JSON as base64 at its original revision.
get_scene_snapshot_chunk.name: get_scene_snapshot_chunk

get_signed_distance_field.description: Samples a bounded world-space signed-distance grid at cell centres against one retained paused snapshot. Distances are metres, negative inside and positive outside. Exact values require one authored analytic box, sphere or cylinder; unions and baked geometry are returned as unknown.
get_signed_distance_field.name: get_signed_distance_field

get_temporal_sample.description: Copies one selected camera and up to 64 selected object poses from a named retained all-systems-paused snapshot.
get_temporal_sample.name: get_temporal_sample

instance_get.description: Every property of one instance, by the id world_tree reported.
instance_get.name: instance_get

instance_set.description: Writes one property of one instance. Vector3 and Color3 take an object of named components; an enum takes its member name as a string.
instance_set.name: instance_set

layer_table.description: The engine's layer stack, bottom to top: every module at each height, with its tier. A layer may see every layer below it and none above it, so this table is what decides which module may include which. The programs are listed separately - they are what links modules and nothing links them. Call module_may_link to ask about one edge.
layer_table.name: layer_table

lifecycle_inspect.description: Reads one data-factory world's completed tick and lifecycle revision without changing it.
lifecycle_inspect.name: lifecycle_inspect

log_level.description: Reads or changes what this program logs, while it runs. With no argument it lists every category the build has registered and the severity floor each is at. `set` takes the same text the engine.log-level setting does: a bare level for everything, or comma-separated category=level overrides, or both - `warning,net=trace`. Statements below the compiled floor were removed by the preprocessor and cannot be switched on.

set.description: A level, or category=level terms, or both.

log_level.name: log_level

log_tail.description: The most recent lines this program has logged, newest last. Filter by minimum level and by category - a category is one area of the engine, usually one module, and log_level lists the ones this build registers. Only the last 1024 lines are kept, and `dropped` says how many scrolled off before the oldest one shown.

category.description: Only lines from this area. Default all of them.

level.description: The lowest severity to include. Default trace.

lines.description: How many lines at most. Default 50, capped at 1024.

log_tail.name: log_tail

metrics_read.description: Every counter, gauge and distribution this process has recorded. A counter accumulates and is drained once a frame, so its value is a rate; a gauge is a level as last set; a histogram carries a mean, a maximum and nearest-rank percentiles over its recent window, which is what says whether a server holding its tick rate on average is still missing a fiftieth of its ticks. Times are nanoseconds. Reading changes nothing.

prefix.description: Only names starting with this. Default all of them.

metrics_read.name: metrics_read

module_get.description: One module or program: which layer and tier it is, every first-party target it links, and everything that links it. `linkedBy` is what would have to be rebuilt and reviewed if this module's interface changed. With no name, every module in layer order.

name.description: The module or program. Omit for all of them.

module_get.name: module_get

module_may_link.description: Whether one module is allowed to link another, and why. This is the question the architecture check answers, decided here from the same two rules: a tier may link shared and its own tier, and a layer may see every layer below it and none above it. Ask before writing an include - an edge that runs upward is refused at configure time and the fix is almost never to widen the rule.
module_may_link.name: module_may_link

negotiate.description: Pure data-factory capability discovery. Reports this host's callable MCP operations and their schemas, and names unsupported proposed capture capabilities instead of guessing from renderer internals. It does not create, load, reset, or mutate a world.
negotiate.name: negotiate

overlap_aabb.description: Return stable authored ids for prepared physics colliders overlapping one finite world-space axis-aligned box.
overlap_aabb.name: overlap_aabb

overlap_obb.description: Return stable authored ids for prepared physics colliders overlapping one finite world-space oriented box.
overlap_obb.name: overlap_obb

pause.description: Pauses one data-factory world at a completed tick boundary.
pause.name: pause

physics_observation_hooks.description: Lists the stable fixed-step physics observation hook names and the completed-record capacity.
physics_observation_hooks.name: physics_observation_hooks

physics_observation_records.description: Returns up to 96 completed fixed-step physics records for one factory-owned world. The hook name declares post-integration, pre-solve, or completed-solver state. Values retain exact tick, physics step, step seconds and availability; unavailable fields are null. The read cannot change physics state.
physics_observation_records.name: physics_observation_records

poll_capture.description: Reads capture metadata without consuming its retained plane bytes.
poll_capture.name: poll_capture

poll_render_only.description: Reads pending, submitted, or failed render-only command status. Submitted does not claim GPU readback readiness.
poll_render_only.name: poll_render_only

poll_view_camera_mutation.description: Returns a view.camera mutation status and releases a terminal mutation ticket.
poll_view_camera_mutation.name: poll_view_camera_mutation

profile_frame.description: The last frame as a flame graph: one span per scope with its depth, its parent, its inclusive time and its self time. Collection is switched on by the first call, so the first reply is empty and the next one is not.
profile_frame.name: profile_frame

raycast.description: Cast a finite ray through one scene's prepared physics colliders and return exact hit metadata with a stable authored entity id when one exists.
raycast.name: raycast

release_capture.description: Releases one terminal capture and its retained bytes.
release_capture.name: release_capture

release_gltf_scene.description: Releases one retained glTF export, including after its world revision changes.
release_gltf_scene.name: release_gltf_scene

release_raw_scene_extract.description: Releases one retained raw scene extract, including after its world revision changes.
release_raw_scene_extract.name: release_raw_scene_extract

release_scene_snapshot.description: Releases one retained scene snapshot, including after its world revision changes.
release_scene_snapshot.name: release_scene_snapshot

render_only.description: Queues one static frame from a paused snapshot. Submitted means the frame command was accepted, not that GPU readback is ready.
render_only.name: render_only

restore.description: Restores a compatible checkpoint through a scratch universe and starts a fresh epoch.
restore.name: restore

resume.description: Resumes one data-factory world at a completed tick boundary.
resume.name: resume

run_script_package.description: Runs one atomic.data-script.v1 package in a fresh capability-limited Luau sandbox and atomically replaces a paused factory world.
run_script_package.name: run_script_package

script_check.description: Type-checks Luau against the engine's generated declarations, without running any of it. Give `source` for a draft or `path` for a file in the repository. Every diagnostic the editor's language server would show comes back here, because both go through the same declaration file. Nothing is evaluated: this surface will not run a script, because a tool runs inside the program's frame and there is nothing here that could interrupt a loop.

path.description: A path relative to the repository root, instead of `source`.

script_check.name: script_check

seek_backward.description: Restores the newest retained paused checkpoint and replays contiguous action-free fixed steps to an earlier completed tick.
seek_backward.name: seek_backward

snapshot.description: Retains one immutable world snapshot at a completed boundary.
snapshot.name: snapshot

step.description: Advances one all-systems-paused world through its canonical dt_ns interval. Nonempty actions are unsupported until the host installs an executor.
step.name: step

submit_view_camera_mutation.description: Queues one owned synchronous view.camera patch for an exact paused snapshot and pipeline revision.
submit_view_camera_mutation.name: submit_view_camera_mutation

visibility_observations.description: Returns bounded per-object facts from the completed main camera submission.
visibility_observations.name: visibility_observations

world_create.description: Creates one factory-owned local world in this Universe.
world_create.name: world_create

world_list.description: Every scene, with its state, its tick statistics and how many instances it holds. A world is a scene; the universe is the game.
world_list.name: world_list

world_reset.description: Resets one factory-owned local world after an all-systems pause.
world_reset.name: world_reset

world_retire.description: Retires one factory-owned local world after an all-systems pause and returns a tombstone.
world_retire.name: world_retire

world_tree.description: The instance tree of one scene, as an author sees it in the explorer. Depth-limited and count-limited; ask for more when you know where you are going.
world_tree.name: world_tree

initialize.instructions: A shipped atomic game client. Its universe contains local scenes and may also contain a replica received from a dedicated server. Replica writes are refused by their store.

headless_cpu.name: headless_cpu
headless_cpu.reason: not declared by this control host

limits.reason: this host does not implement the data-factory operation

atomic://architecture/layers.description: Every module by height, with the rule that decides which may include which. ReadResourceFile this before adding an include across modules.
atomic://architecture/layers.name: The layer stack

atomic://architecture/modules.description: Every module and program as JSON: tier, layer, what it links, what links it, and the sideways edges each is allowed. The same data the architecture check enforces.
atomic://architecture/modules.name: The module graph

atomic://bindings/luau.description: The type declarations every Luau script in this engine is checked against, and the file script_check uses.
atomic://bindings/luau.name: The Luau declarations

atomic://bindings/manifest.description: Every class, property, enum and datatype a script may name, generated from the class table by `just bindings`. Large - a couple of hundred kilobytes.
atomic://bindings/manifest.name: The scripting manifest

atomic://components.description: Every component type this engine registers, with its size, whether it is a tag, whether a save file can carry it and how many bytes a replication delta needs.
atomic://components.name: The component catalogue

class_get.description: One class: what it derives from, and every property it exposes with the type it carries, whether it can be written and whether a script can see it at all. This is the live class table rather than the checked-in manifest, so it describes what this process registered. Use instance_get to read the values off a particular instance.
class_get.name: class_get

class_list.description: Every class this process registers, with what it derives from. A class is what Instance.new names and what a save file carries; its properties are what a script may read and write. Inheritance is set inclusion here, so a query for a base class matches every derived instance. Call class_get for one class's properties.

derivedFrom.description: Only classes that are a kind of this one.

class_list.name: class_list

component_get.description: The values one entity holds for one component, field by field. Null when the entity does not carry it - which is a different answer from carrying it with every field at zero.
component_get.name: component_get

component_list.description: Every component a game declared for itself, with its fields and how many entities in a scene carry it. A component is the storage under the class tree: an instance is an entity and a class is a set of these. Components the engine declares are not listed here - those are reached as properties, through instance_get.
component_list.name: component_list

component_set.description: Writes fields of one component on one entity, adding it when the entity does not carry it yet. Fields left out keep what they had; a fresh component starts at zero. Vector3 and Color3 take an object of named components, as instance_set does.
component_set.name: component_set

engine_components.description: Every component type this engine registers, with its size, whether it is a tag, whether a save file can carry it and whether replication has a compact form for it. A component is the storage under the class tree: an instance is an entity and a class is a set of these. Use component_list instead for the components a game declared for itself, and instance_get to read one off a particular instance.
engine_components.name: engine_components

engine_info.description: This program's own state: how many scenes it holds and what they are called. Call it first.
engine_info.name: engine_info

entity_query.description: Every entity in a scene carrying all of the named components. This is the query a system runs, asked from outside: name the components and get the ids back, then read one with component_get or instance_get.

components.description: Every one an entity must carry. Call component_list first.

entity_query.name: entity_query

instance_get.description: Every property of one instance, by the id world_tree reported.
instance_get.name: instance_get

instance_set.description: Writes one property of one instance. Vector3 and Color3 take an object of named components; an enum takes its member name as a string.
instance_set.name: instance_set

layer_table.description: The engine's layer stack, bottom to top: every module at each height, with its tier. A layer may see every layer below it and none above it, so this table is what decides which module may include which. The programs are listed separately - they are what links modules and nothing links them. Call module_may_link to ask about one edge.
layer_table.name: layer_table

log_level.description: Reads or changes what this program logs, while it runs. With no argument it lists every category the build has registered and the severity floor each is at. `set` takes the same text the engine.log-level setting does: a bare level for everything, or comma-separated category=level overrides, or both - `warning,net=trace`. Statements below the compiled floor were removed by the preprocessor and cannot be switched on.

set.description: A level, or category=level terms, or both.

log_level.name: log_level

log_tail.description: The most recent lines this program has logged, newest last. Filter by minimum level and by category - a category is one area of the engine, usually one module, and log_level lists the ones this build registers. Only the last 1024 lines are kept, and `dropped` says how many scrolled off before the oldest one shown.

category.description: Only lines from this area. Default all of them.

level.description: The lowest severity to include. Default trace.

lines.description: How many lines at most. Default 50, capped at 1024.

log_tail.name: log_tail

metrics_read.description: Every counter, gauge and distribution this process has recorded. A counter accumulates and is drained once a frame, so its value is a rate; a gauge is a level as last set; a histogram carries a mean, a maximum and nearest-rank percentiles over its recent window, which is what says whether a server holding its tick rate on average is still missing a fiftieth of its ticks. Times are nanoseconds. Reading changes nothing.

prefix.description: Only names starting with this. Default all of them.

metrics_read.name: metrics_read

module_get.description: One module or program: which layer and tier it is, every first-party target it links, and everything that links it. `linkedBy` is what would have to be rebuilt and reviewed if this module's interface changed. With no name, every module in layer order.

name.description: The module or program. Omit for all of them.

module_get.name: module_get

module_may_link.description: Whether one module is allowed to link another, and why. This is the question the architecture check answers, decided here from the same two rules: a tier may link shared and its own tier, and a layer may see every layer below it and none above it. Ask before writing an include - an edge that runs upward is refused at configure time and the fix is almost never to widen the rule.
module_may_link.name: module_may_link

negotiate.description: Pure data-factory capability discovery. Reports this host's callable MCP operations and their schemas, and names unsupported proposed capture capabilities instead of guessing from renderer internals. It does not create, load, reset, or mutate a world.
negotiate.name: negotiate

profile_frame.description: The last frame as a flame graph: one span per scope with its depth, its parent, its inclusive time and its self time. Collection is switched on by the first call, so the first reply is empty and the next one is not.
profile_frame.name: profile_frame

script_check.description: Type-checks Luau against the engine's generated declarations, without running any of it. Give `source` for a draft or `path` for a file in the repository. Every diagnostic the editor's language server would show comes back here, because both go through the same declaration file. Nothing is evaluated: this surface will not run a script, because a tool runs inside the program's frame and there is nothing here that could interrupt a loop.

path.description: A path relative to the repository root, instead of `source`.

script_check.name: script_check

visibility_observations.description: Returns bounded per-object facts from the completed main camera submission.
visibility_observations.name: visibility_observations

world_list.description: Every scene, with its state, its tick statistics and how many instances it holds. A world is a scene; the universe is the game.
world_list.name: world_list

world_tree.description: The instance tree of one scene, as an author sees it in the explorer. Depth-limited and count-limited; ask for more when you know where you are going.
world_tree.name: world_tree
